summary: Procurement and legal review for HarborTech vendor onboarding. Discussed MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs (latency/uptime), pricing approval path, dedicated vs hosted deployment options, encryption/KMS and SOC2 artifacts. Agreed next steps and timelines for redlines and a technical bakeoff.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 56 minutes | Attendees: James Porter, Sasha Li (Redwood); Maya Rodriguez, Ethan Cole, Priya Nair, Leo Kim (HarborTech)

[00:00] James: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm James Porter from Redwood - I'm the AE on this account. Sasha, do you want to intro?
[00:15] Sasha: Yeah hey all, Sasha Li, solutions engineer. We'll run through the MSA/DPA points, the SLA asks, and then map next steps for legal and procurement.
[00:29] Maya: Great thanks. We have a short timeline, procurement wants approval this month, legal needs to get redlines in by next week ideally.
[00:41] James: Understood. Quick check - Priya, from security, any immediate hard blocks we should know about?
[00:47] Priya: We need KMS integration for customer-managed keys, SOC2 report, and confirmation about data residency — some of our data must stay in EU region. Also need audit logs retention and RBAC controls.
[01:05] Sasha: Okay, that's good. We support KMS integrations, HSM options in Private deployments, and we can pin region for data residency in Dedicated or Private. The SOC2 bundle and ISO artifacts we can share.
[01:22] Ethan: On the MSA, we flagged the indemnity and liability caps, and want clearer language around service credits for SLA breaches.
[01:33] James: Sure. Our standard is 99.95% uptime for Dedicated with tiered service credits — we can lay out the exact table. For Hosted, the SLA is lower.
[01:45] Leo: Can you clarify Hosted vs Dedicated cost delta? Procurement needs ballpark numbers tied to throughput.
[01:52] James: Absolutely. We'll send a pricing sheet but rough numbers: Hosted is pay-as-you-go and typically lower TCO for low to medium usage. Dedicated is reserved capacity, higher commit cost but predictable latency and isolation — better for high query volumes. Sasha can give more detail.
[02:10] Sasha: Right. Example: for sustained throughput of 100 req/s with 2k token responses, Dedicated with pinned GPU pool is usually more cost-effective. We have quantization and batching options to reduce unit cost too.
[02:30] Maya: For procurement signoff we need: signed MSA/DPA, SLA table, SOC2 artifacts, and a single point price for year one. Also we prefer annual billing.
[02:43] James: We can align annual billing. We'll create a SOW for year one commitment.
[02:50] Ethan: On DPA, we may need EU SCCs — do you accept those? Also need to confirm data deletion timelines after contract termination.
[02:59] Sasha: We can include standard SCCs in the DPA and outline deletion timelines; for Dedicated/Private we can guarantee return or deletion per the DPA. I'll note that as a redline point.
[03:15] Priya: One more security item, we want to validate that there are no model weights retention policies that would cause customer data to be used for training.
[03:25] Sasha: Redwood's hosted models are not trained on customer inputs; we can provide the language. For Private deployments it's customer-managed so it's isolated.
[03:36] Speaker 1: (mumble) question about network egress costs.
[03:40] James: Good question — for Dedicated, network egress is handled in the commit; for Hosted it's per-GB. We'll include estimates.
[03:50] Maya: Regarding SLAs, our bar for mission-critical features is 99.9% at minimum and we want latency SLOs 95th pctl < 200ms for short prompts. Is that realistic?
[04:04] Sasha: 200ms 95th is aggressive for some open models depending on sequence length and model size. On Dedicated with GPU optimized runtime we can approach that for small seqs, but for larger seqs latency increases. We should scope which endpoints are mission-critical.
[04:24] Leo: We're primarily looking at embeddings and short chat completions for the first phase, so mostly short seqs.
[04:31] Sasha: That helps. We'll propose SLOs per route: embeddings, chat-short, chat-long.
[04:40] Ethan: Penalty language — we need clear service credits matrix and an upper cap on credits.
[04:47] James: Our standard is a percentage of monthly committed fees as credits; we can propose a matrix and negotiate caps.
[04:54] Maya: Procurement will also need vendor risk questionnaire answers. Can you provide the standard VRQ packet?
[05:01] James: Yes we'll share that.
[05:06] [05:06] Sasha: I'll add the VRQ and SOC2 artifacts to the shared folder. Link: (sent in chat) 
[05:12] Maya: Thanks.
[05:15] [05:15] Ethan: On pricing approval — our finance team needs a one-page cost summary with scenarios (low/medium/high usage) and a recommended commit.
[05:25] James: We can produce that and include delta Hosted vs Dedicated and the SOW for year one.
[05:31] Priya: For KMS, we need to confirm support for AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault, and whether keys are in our account or managed by Redwood.
[05:41] Sasha: For Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS in customer's cloud account. For Hosted, we offer a Redwood-managed KMS but we can discuss bring-your-own-key in enterprise arrangements.
[05:56] Maya: Great. Timeline — procurement wants to finish redlines by next Friday. Is that doable?
[06:02] James: Yes, we can aim for that. We'll return a redline-ready MSA and DPA draft in 3 business days.
[06:09] Leo: For the technical bakeoff — we'd like a week-long run with our sample workload and Redwood to run benchmarks for Hosted and Dedicated. Can you support that?
[06:18] Sasha: Definitely. We'll provide the runbook and can schedule it the week of 3/22. We request sample data and traffic patterns.
[06:26] Ethan: On legal side, there are two clauses to be careful with — termination for convenience notice period and data return obligations.
[06:35] James: We typically have 30-90 day notice options; we can discuss a clause that fits HarborTech's procurement policies.
[06:42] Priya: Another item: audit rights. We need to understand if we can audit Redwood or get third-party SOC attestations.
[06:49] Sasha: We offer SOC2 Type II reports and can support reasonably scoped audits via standard procedures; full audits are handled via channels and require coordination.
[06:59] Maya: Competitors we've evaluated — Anthropic and MajorCloudAI — highlighted pricing but lacked dedicated deployment options in our evaluation. That matters for our security posture.
[07:12] James: Good to know. We can highlight Dedicated and Private options in the SOW.
[07:18] [07:18] James: Quick recap of agreements: Redwood to send redline-ready MSA/DPA, pricing sheet and SOW, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and benchmark runbook. HarborTech to return MSA redlines and KMS requirements. Schedule bakeoff week of 3/22.
[07:35] Maya: Sounds right. One more question: who will be our day-to-day Redwood contact during onboarding?
[07:42] James: That will be me for procurement/contract, and Sasha will lead the technical onboarding. We'll introduce the CSM once onboarding begins.
[07:51] Ethan: Thanks. We'll aim to get redlines to you by 3/19.
[07:55] James: Great. I'll follow up with the documents and a calendar invite for the bakeoff planning session.
[08:02] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[08:05] Leo: Thanks.
[08:08] James: Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription contains a couple of mis-heard snippets (Speaker 1 mumble), some vendor/product names abbreviated. Links shared in chat: SOC2 bundle (link), VRQ packet (link), Pricing sheet (placeholder link).

Action summary (from call):
- Redwood to deliver MSA/DPA redline-ready drafts and pricing/SOW (James)
- Redwood to share SOC2/ISO artifacts and VRQ (Sasha)
- Redwood to provide benchmark runbook and schedule bakeoff (Sasha)
- HarborTech to provide MSA redlines and KMS requirements (Ethan/Priya)

End of transcript.
